A-33 As is customary with many universities across the country, a five percent one-time gift fee is deducted from donations to provide essential support to the University’s overall development activities.
As of July 1, 2021, this fee became applicable only to non-endowed donations.
The University’s endowment represents a permanent partnership between the University, the URI Foundation and the generous endowment benefactors.
The General Endowment Fund (“GEF”) of the University of Rhode Island Foundation is a pool of approximately 1,280 permanently endowed, named funds, the majority of which provide scholarship funding for undergraduate and graduate students at URI.
The Foundation’s main objective in managing and investing the GEF is to generate a consistent income stream for distributi on to the University in accordance with the donor’s wishes, while protecting and growing the endowment’s principal value.
A portion of the endowment’s earnings and appreciation is reinvested into the GEF each year.
The URI Foundation’s spending rate, as es tablished by its Executive Board, was 5.05% for fiscal year 20 25.

This rate includes both the University distribution and the Foundation’s management fee.
The distribution to the University equaled 3.6% of the preceding twelve quarter rolling average market value of the endowment up to and including December 31, 2023, which resulted in a disbursement to the University of $7.53 million.
As of June 30, 2025, the University of Rhode Island’s endowment portfolio had a market value of $266.9 million, up 13% f rom $237.2 million the previous year.
The Foundation’s benchmark is the 70% MSCI ACWI/30% BBG Aggregate index; the return was 13.2% for the same period.
The Foundation also holds $11.8 million outside of the endowment pool separately for statutory purposes or to comply with donor intent.
The Alumni Engagement office of URI Foundation & Alumni Engagement strengthens alumni ties to and promotes interest in the University through events, reunions, and communications.
Alumni Engagement has increasingly built p rogramming that targets specific demographics according to geographic location, career, degree, and affinity.

President DATE: October 27, 2005 SUBJECT: Action Item: Approval of a Contract in excess of $5 Million, Nexgen Mechanical Inc.
P urpose of Submittal: The purpose of this action item is to seek Board of Trustees approval, under the Policy on Approval and Execution of Contracts and Other Binding Documents, of a change order to the Facilities Operations contract with Nexgen Mechanical Inc.
This contract represents ongoing support services which are part of the current operations of the campus for service and repair to the University’s chillers and HVAC systems.
This contract was previously approved by the Board in November of 2023 for $6M over three years.
The proposed increase of $2.9M to the contract value will cover additional anticipated critical repairs and scheduled maintenance.
R ecommendation: It is recommended that the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees approve the proposed Change Order to the Nexgen Contract.

P oints to Consider: This contract was initially approved by the Board of Trustees in November of 2023 as a three -year contract through June 30, 2026, with a contract value estimated at $6 million.
The original contract assumed an annual spend of $1.5M, but did not adequately taking into account unanticipated emergency repairs and required equipment replacement, and less than $500,000 currently now remains available on the contract.
T o meet the HVAC and chiller maintenance and repair needs for the University though the balance of this year, the university would need at minimum an additional $2.4M added to the contract value.
With prudence to account for unanticipated emergencies, the university is requesting a contract increase of $2.9M.
T he University’s Facilities Operations group is presently working with URI Purchasing to maximize contracting options for HVAC equipment replacement , due to life -cycle failures and other forecasted needs , and preventative maintenance and repair.
Separating this work should result in a broader range of vendor options, which will allow us to better negotiate set pricing and establish tighter budget controls.
We anticipate this new contract framework to be in place by July 2026.
